**Composition**

work-unit · 2026-08-23

Discharges: [MUS-M-0007](../milestones.md#mus-m-0007)

Decided by: [MUS-D-0096](../decisions.md#mus-d-0096)

And by: [MUS-D-0097](../decisions.md#mus-d-0097)

## Context

The composer the phone exists for: multi-line, spell-checked, drafted, and reaching the session it names. Built into the session view rather than as a page of its own, because a second scripted surface is a decision and this one already carries the client layer.

## Done means

The composer is a textarea, spell-checked, autocapitalised and autocorrected, growing with what is typed to a cap and scrolling after it.
Enter inserts a newline; the Send button submits, and on a desktop so does Ctrl or Cmd with Enter.
A draft survives a reload, a dropped connection and a backgrounded phone, under one key rather than one per session, and the surface says it is being kept.
The destination is named above the box and changing it does not cost the draft.
Multi-line text arrives in the session as one message rather than as one prompt per line.
A send that could not go leaves the draft where it was.

## Verified against

Real tmux and the real CLI, plus tests.

The clause no test proves: that a bracketed paste reaches an agent's composer as ONE message rather than one prompt per line. Measured by hand against Claude Code — four lines pasted into a live pane, one Enter, and the agent answered from all four, replying 'ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE' to a message whose first three lines were those words. The same check with plain send-keys also placed all four lines in the composer, which is why the mechanism is argued from reliability rather than from a failure to work.

What the tests do prove: multi-line leaves the composer over a real WebSocket and arrives in a real session's input, in order, newlines intact (TestMultiLineFromTheComposerReachesTheSession); Send uses the bracketed, self-cleaning paste path for multi-line and keystrokes for single-line (fake-runner tests, where the command line is visible); the surface renders a spell-checked textarea with a named destination and a draft indicator; and the draft key is a constant rather than per-project.

Neither real-tmux test discriminates between paste and keystrokes, because the pane holds cat and cat is happy with newlines either way. That is stated in the test rather than left for a reader to discover.

## Risks

The done-when says from a phone, off the home network, without a terminal. The transport, the multi-line handling and the draft are verified; the phone, the network and the browser's spell-checker are the owner's to confirm, as 2c's last sentence was.

Enter-inserts-newline is a change in feel from the single-line box that shipped at 4b, where Enter sent. Nobody has used the new one yet.

The draft lives in the browser, so it is per-device: a draft started on the phone is not on the laptop. That is the cost of holding no per-client state on the server, which the stack table requires.
